summary.name: Fossil
summary.one_liner: Fossil is a distributed version control system that bundles bug tracking, wiki, forum, chat and a built-in web interface in a single executable.
use_cases: track bugs and tickets alongside code
run a project website with wiki and forum
version control over weak or firewalled networks
host a small project on a cheap VPS or Raspberry Pi
keep source history in a single portable file
summary.what_it_does: Fossil is a distributed source control system that supports version control like Git and Mercurial, plus bug tracking, a wiki, a forum, email alerts, chat and technotes. It includes a built-in, themeable web interface, and the project's own website is a running Fossil instance. Repositories are stored in SQLite, and automatic self-checks verify consistency before each commit. Network sync uses HTTPS or SSH, and the project states that most projects can be hosted on a $5/month VPS or a Raspberry Pi. The current release listed is 2.28 (2026-03-11).
notable: Single self-contained executable with built-in web UI
Bundles bug tracking, wiki, forum, chat and technotes with version control
Uses HTTPS or SSH, works behind firewalls and proxies
Stores repositories in SQLite with atomic transactions and self-checks
caveats: Source code is available to compile, but the page does not describe a paid tier
